2027-02-12.title: Friday of the first week of the Great Fast
readings: The God who sees Hagar in the wilderness
The law written on their hearts
Everyone who acknowledges me before others
2027-02-12.verse: And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God;
theo: Yesterday Hagar ran away into the wilderness. Today “the angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness” and asks two questions that every soul in the Fast should hear: “Hagar, slave-girl of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?” She can answer only the first: “I am running away.” God sends her back, but not empty: he promises her a son and names him Ishmael, “for the Lord has given heed to your affliction.” And Hagar, the foreign slave whom no one else noticed, does what almost no one else in Scripture dares: she gives God a name of her own: “You are El-roi,” the God who sees. “Have I really seen God and remained alive after seeing him?” On a Friday of the Fast we remember that the God who sees is the God who looked down from the Cross on all the afflicted.

Paul says that God sees the heart of every human being, not only of those who have the written law: Gentiles “show that what the law requires is written on their hearts, to which their own conscience also bears witness,” on the day “when, according to my gospel, God, through Jesus Christ, will judge the secret thoughts of all.” The Fast is a time to let that light into our secret thoughts. In the Gospel Jesus asks for courage in the open: “everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God.” When we are brought before authorities, we need not worry: “the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.” The God who sees Hagar in the wilderness also stands beside those who confess him before the world.
outline: Ask: where have you come from, and where are you going?
The Spirit will teach you what to say.
live: Tonight write two lines: where have I come from in my life, and where am I going?
Make an honest examination of conscience today and plan a good confession during the Fast.
2027-02-12.prayer: Lord, you are the God who sees. You found Hagar by the spring in the wilderness and heard her affliction. See us in our wilderness, search our secret thoughts, and heal what you find there. Give us courage to acknowledge your Son before others, and teach us by your Holy Spirit what to say. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Lord who sees our affliction offers himself on the altar for all, near and far.

quick: The angel of the Lord found Hagar in the wilderness; she named God “the God who sees.”
God's law is written on human hearts; conscience bears witness.
Jesus promises to acknowledge those who acknowledge him before others.
2027-02-12.action: Make an honest examination of conscience tonight.
2027-02-12.question: Where have I come from, and where am I going?

family.explain: Hagar was alone and frightened in the desert. But God found her and spoke to her. She called God “the God who sees me.” God sees each of us too, always, and he cares.
family.intention: We pray for people who are lonely, runaways and refugees.
family.ask: Ask: “When did I feel that God saw me and helped me?”

illus: A social worker in Kottayam who runs a shelter for women says the first words she hears from most newcomers are: no one knew what was happening to me. She keeps a small sign in Malayalam above the door of the shelter: the God who sees me. One woman told her later: when I read that, I cried for the first time in years. I realised someone had been watching over me all along.

pm.open: God who sees, look upon us in our wilderness and lead us home. Amen.
share: Where have you come from and where are you going? (Genesis 16:8). How would I answer?
Written on their hearts (Romans 2:15). What is my conscience telling me in this Fast?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). Where do I hesitate to acknowledge Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, you see us; have mercy on us.
interc: For women and children who suffer harsh treatment at home.
For those who follow their conscience without knowing Christ.
For Christians brought before courts and authorities because of their faith.
For all who will make a confession during this Fast.
pm.close: Father, you saw Hagar in the wilderness and heard her affliction. See every suffering person today, and through the Cross of your Son bring them home. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hagar ran away into the wilderness. The angel of the Lord found her by a spring and asked: where have you come from and where are you going? (Genesis 16:8). In this first week of the Fast, God asks us the same.
God heard her affliction, and Hagar named him: You are El-roi, the God who sees (Genesis 16:11, 13). No one is invisible to God.
Paul says that God's law is written even on the hearts of those who have not heard it, and their conscience bears witness (Romans 2:15). In the Fast we let God's light into our secret thoughts.

And Jesus says: everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God (Luke 12:8). On this Friday, let us not hide our faith, and let us trust the Spirit to teach us what to say. Amen.
kids: Children, Hagar was alone in the desert, but God found her! She called him “the God who sees me.” God sees you too, always, and he loves you.

intro: Theme: “Everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God.”
The God who sees Hagar, the law written on the heart, and courage to confess Christ.

sub: Found by a spring in the wilderness.
Where have you come from, where are you going?
q: So she named the Lord who spoke to her, “You are El-roi”; for she said, “Have I really seen God and remained alive after seeing him?”
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in hidden prayer each day of the Fast.

q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
They show that what the law requires is written on their hearts, to which their own conscience also bears witness;
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience and go to confession.

sub: The Spirit teaches what to say.
q: The Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.
points.apply: Speak of your faith openly in one conversation this week.

concl: No one is invisible to the God who sees.
He who sees our hearts gives us courage to confess his Son.
2027-02-12.resolve: Make a good confession before the middle of the Fast.
